KITCHEN LESSON · KITCHEN THINGS · AGES 3–6 YEARS

Trash Bin — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson teaches the trash bin as mess’s destination: pedal opens the lid, in it goes, close. And the scraps-bowl job after dinner is the easiest real chore in the house.

What is this?

A trash bin is the gray pedal bin with the green lid — the place wrappers and peels go, operated by the best foot-button in the kitchen.

What does it mean?

A named bin gives mess an address — halving the "where does this go?" questions. The pedal works by foot, so hands stay clean and the lid feels like magic.

What does the child need to know?

You need the bin and the pedal-toss: step, open, in, close. Then the promotion: carrying the little scraps bowl after dinner — one trip, one job, owned.

Why this matters

Bin jobs scale perfectly: pedal-toss at two, scraps-bowl at three, bin-day carrying at five. The first chore in the house is a foot pedal away.

What it teaches

Foot-pedal coordination, aim-and-drop, the tidy-as-we-go habit, and chore pride that scales with the child.

Words to learn

trash binpedallidin it goesscrapstidy

Say this to your child

“"Trash bin! Step on the pedal — the lid opens! In it goes… close. You are the bin chief: wrappers, peels, paper — pedal, toss, close! And after dinner, the scraps bowl rides to the bin. Two hands. What a helper!"”

Step by step

  1. Demo the magic: "trash bin! Step on the pedal… the lid opens — whoosh! In it goes… close."
  2. The job title: "you are the bin chief — every wrapper goes in by YOUR pedal."
  3. The round: cooking wrappers, paper towels, apple skins — pedal, toss, close, each one named.
  4. The promotion: "after dinner, the scraps bowl goes to the bin — carry it with two hands!"
  5. The close: lid down, hands washed — "the bin chief keeps the kitchen clean!"

Look closer at the picture

On this card the words "trash bin" sit over a gray pedal bin with a green lid — the pedal at the front, waiting for a small foot.

Ask your child

"Where do wrappers go?" (in the bin!) "What opens the lid?" (the pedal — your foot!) "Whose job is the scraps bowl?" (the bin chief — me!)

What your child can say or do

Your child might pedal-toss everything (sweet wrappers, hopes), carry the scraps bowl nightly, or refuse bins without pedals — the chore, claimed.

Out in the real world

Bins pedal and swing in every kitchen, park and classroom. "Where does this go? The bin!" scales to every mess the child will ever meet.

Try it together

Bin Hoops: soft wrappers tossed from a step back — pedal, aim, SCORE. Baskets counted; the kitchen tidies itself between quarters.

Understanding check

Ask: "Where does mess go?" (the trash bin) "What opens the lid?" (the pedal) "What is the after-dinner job?" (the scraps bowl!)

This lesson pairs with the Trash Bin flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Kitchen Things.
